MOT T cell line can induce B cell activation and differentiation in vitro.
the transformed T cell line MOT is a useful tool to induce B cell proliferation and immunoglobulin secretion from peripheral blood, splenic and tumor-infiltration lymphocytes.
the use of MOT cells as a source of B cell growth factors is an efficient and practical way to obtain polyclonal B cells for the study of B cell responses in humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a T cell line that can be used to study human B cell responses.
the use of transformed T lymphocytes as a source of helper activity for B cell responses.
the development of a system to expand and study B cells from patients with cancer and HIV infection.

MOT cells are able to activate B cells in vitro from normal peripheral blood, spleens from HIV+ individuals, and TIL from three different tumor types, and are thus a useful tool to study B cell activation and differentiation.
MOT is the best of the T cell lines we have tested for the induction of B cell responses.
the use of transformed T cells is an effective method to expand and activate B cells from peripheral and tumor sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transformed T cell lines can be used to expand human B cells from different sources for the study of antigen-specific responses and for the development of new therapeutic approaches.
transformed T cells can be used as a source of B cell activators and immunoglobulin secretors for the study of B cell function in normal and neoplastic tissues.
transformed T cell lines are a useful tool for the clonal expansion of B cells from peripheral and tumor-infiltrated lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transformed T cell lines can be used to induce B cell proliferation and immunoglobulin secretion in a variety of human cells.
MOT is a potent polyclonal activator of B cells from peripheral B cells, spleen, or tumor-infiltrating B cells.
MOT cells are able to induce B cell responses from a wide variety of sources, and therefore can be useful for the study of human B cell responses in vivo.
